title: Chiral-symmetry breaking and degeneracy in Koch fractal geometries
abstract: Fractal geometries provide a distinctive platform for controlling quantum interference, topology, and localization. We investigate the Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) model constructed on the Koch curve, where a triangular geometry enables additional same-sublattice hoppings that break chiral symmetry and modify the conventional topological behavior captured by a real-space local marker. Destructive interference within the triangular units produces a highly degenerate flat level at $E=-t$. Although this level originates from the local geometry, its degeneracy and spectral weight are controlled by the self-similar connectivity of the Koch curve. The hierarchy reduces the number of independent flat states and reorganizes the spectrum into an intricate distribution of energy levels. Our results reveal complementary roles for local triangular interference and global fractal connectivity in shaping the electronic properties of geometrically modified SSH chains.
summary: This work examines the electronic structure of the SSH model placed on a Koch fractal lattice. By introducing local triangular hoppings, the model develops a degenerate flat band, while the global fractal connectivity of the Koch curve systematically reduces this degeneracy. The findings highlight a crucial interplay between local geometric features and global fractal structure in determining quantum electronic properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates how coupling the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model to the geometry of the Koch fractal modifies its topological properties and electronic spectrum.
main_result: The local triangular geometry creates a highly degenerate flat band at E=-t, but the global fractal connectivity of the Koch curve reduces this degeneracy and alters the spectral weight compared to a simple extended chain.
method: The study uses a real-space formulation of the Hamiltonian, analyzing spectral properties, topological markers, and localization via the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
model_or_system: The system is the SSH model constructed on the Koch curve, incorporating additional intra-sublattice hopping terms (t') that break chiral symmetry. The Hamiltonian is analyzed by comparing its behavior to the standard SSH chain.
key_observables: Spectral gaps (E_gap), degeneracy of the flat level at E=-t, local topological marker C(R), and the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
important_parameters: Dimerization parameter (delta t/t) and the chiral-breaking hopping parameter (t'/t).
main_assumptions: Periodic boundary conditions are imposed for bulk-like behavior, and the analysis separates local (triangular) and global (fractal) effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy gap dependence on dimerization and chiral-breaking terms, and show the evolution of the degeneracy of the flat band at E=-t for prolonged versus Koch structures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian, first establishing the role of local triangular hoppings in creating flat bands, then analyzing how the global Koch hierarchy modifies the degeneracy of these states, and finally examining the impact of chiral symmetry breaking.
why_interesting: The combination of fractal geometry, topological models (SSH), and symmetry breaking provides a rich platform for studying how geometric constraints dictate fundamental quantum properties like localization and spectral structure.

Fig. 1(a) illustrates the self-similar construction of the Koch–SSH chain. The triangles generated at successive iterations bring nonconsecutive sites into close spatial proximity, allowing additional hopping terms across the bases of the triangles. To preserve the alternating hop- ping sequence and suppress end-induced finite-size ef- fects, we impose periodic boundary conditions by con- necting sites (N) and (1). Since site (N) belongs to sublattice (B), and site (1) belongs to sublattice (A), the closing bond has amplitude t + δt, thus preserving the dimerization pattern.
